questions.q: What is the primary strategy for determining the meaning of a key word in a poem when a dictionary definition is insufficient?
questions.a: The primary strategy is to analyze the immediate linguistic context (surrounding words, syntax) and the broader thematic context (the poem's subject, tone, imagery) to infer the word's connotative meaning. A wrong answer that says "look it up in a dictionary" reveals the student relies solely on denotative meaning and misses the poetic nuance that context provides.

questions.q: In the line "valqou ty lhafp&lhafp] izse&csfy cks;h", the word "csfy" is glossed as "izse dh csy". Explain in your own words why the poet might have chosen the compound "izse&csfy" instead of just "izse".
questions.a: The compound "izse&csfy" (evening-shadow) evokes a specific visual and temporal atmosphere – the lengthening shadows of evening – which "izse" alone (evening) does not. It suggests a lingering, fading light that mirrors the poem's mood of longing. A wrong answer that says "they mean the same thing" shows the student does not grasp how compound words in Hindi poetry compress imagery and emotion.

questions.q: Given the line "nfèk efFk ?k`r dkf<+ fy;ks] Mkfj n;h Nks;h", use context clues to deduce the meaning of "Nks;h" and explain how it contrasts with "fy;ks" in the same line.
questions.a: "Nks;h" (from glossary: NkN, lkjghu va'k) means a deep, resonant sound or cry, while "fy;ks" means to speak/say. The contrast highlights the intensity of the moment: ordinary speech ("fy;ks") versus a primal, heart-wrenching cry ("Nks;h"). A wrong answer that defines "Nks;h" merely as "sound" misses the emotional weight and the deliberate contrast the poet creates.

questions.q: Compare the effect of the word pair "eksj&eqoqQV" (in the first line) with "yksd&ykt" (in the second line). How do these compound words reflect two different worlds in the poem?
questions.a: "eksj&eqoqQV" (beloved's playful gestures) conveys intimate, personal romance, while "yksd&ykt" (folk/simple, natural) evokes a communal, rustic simplicity. Together they juxtapose the private world of love with the public world of folk tradition. A wrong answer that treats them as mere adjectives fails to see the structural contrast the poet builds between elite courtly culture and folk authenticity.

questions.q: Critique the following student interpretation: "The word 'foyks;h' (glossed as eFkh) simply means happiness, so the line 'nwèk dh eFkfu;k¡ cM+s izse ls foyks;h' means new happinesses are sheltered from the big evening." Is this interpretation adequate? Why or why not?
questions.a: The interpretation is inadequate because "foyks;h" in context means "shelter/protection" (eFkh) not "happiness". The line actually means "the joys of the new (bride) are sheltered/protected from the great evening (of life's sorrows)". The student confused the gloss "eFkh" (which is the meaning of foyks;h) with the word "eFkfu;k¡" (joys). This reveals a failure to distinguish between the key word and its gloss, and to parse the grammatical structure.

questions.q: Create a two-line Hindi couplet (dohe) using at least two key words from the poem (e.g., dkfu, csfy, foyks;h, Nks;h) that captures the poem's theme of love transcending social barriers. Explain your word choices.
questions.a: A good answer would produce a couplet like: "dkfu bhul jaat sab, csfy base man maah; foyks;h mile prem ko, jagat mein yehi raah." And explain: "dkfu" (folk song) represents the voice of the people, "csfy" (evening shadow) symbolizes the fading of rigid norms, "foyks;h" (shelter) shows love's protection. A poor answer would use the words mechanically without connecting them to the theme, showing superficial engagement.
